Its **expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar g}B$ and its **shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\bar g$.

derivations.claim: The pullback cut metric satisfies partial_lambda q_AB=B_AB+B_BA because the transported coordinate fields commute with the affine flow and the connection is torsion-free. The screen/cut identification and the determinant derivative give partial_lambda mu_epsilon,lambda=theta_epsilon mu_epsilon,lambda. At epsilon=0, B_0=0 fixes dA_0 independent of lambda. Smoothness and compactness justify differentiation under the integral, so delta A'=integral_C delta-theta dA_0.

Integrating the adopted first-order focusing ODE from lambda to R and taking R to infinity uses the supplied boundary condition and absolute tail convergence to give delta-theta(lambda,y)=8 pi G_N integral_lambda^infinity delta-T_kk(v,y) dv.
Substituting step 1.2 into step 1.1 yields delta A'(u)=8 pi G_N integral_C dA_0 integral_u^infinity delta-T_kk(v,y) dv.

The absolute first moment bounds the integral of |delta A'|, so delta A(R) has a finite limit. Absolute integrability permits Fubini; integrating step 2.1 from lambda to infinity and evaluating the inner interval length integral_lambda^v du=v-lambda proves delta A_infinity-delta A(lambda)=8 pi G_N M_lambda.
Dividing step 3.1 by 4G_N>0 gives the 2 pi weighted-moment normalization. This is a signed geometric identity, not an entropy or modular-energy statement.
